question: Reheating cream pastries to 100°C for 30 minutes is sufficient to prevent staphylococcal food poisoning because it kills all S. aureus organisms and destroys their enterotoxins.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. While boiling kills S. aureus organisms, their enterotoxins are heat-stable — surviving 100°C for 30 minutes. Once the toxin is preformed in food, no amount of reheating inactivates it. This is the commonest pitfall in outbreak investigation.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is a dangerous misconception. Staphylococcal enterotoxins (SE A–E) are heat-stable and withstand boiling for 30 minutes. Reheating kills the bacteria (cultures may be negative) but the preformed toxin remains fully active and causes illness.
